newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia slashes taxes in surprise budget plan.
newsitem.headline: Zambia slashes taxes in surprise budget plan.

text.p: The Zambian government on Friday announced a surprise cut in Value Added Tax to 17.5 percent from 20 percent.
It also said it would maintain social sector spending, which analysts had predicted would be cut, at last year's level.

"Given our commitment to promoting private sector led growth ... I have reduced VAT to 17.5 percent. This measure will be with effect from July 1, 1997, in keeping with the VAT year," finance minister Ronald Penza said in his national budget speech on Friday.
"Equally important, corrections have been made in the classification of goods for the customs tariff purposes which will result in additional tax relief to the business community," he added.
Analysts had predicted tax increases and cuts in social spending in 1997 as the government strived to secure adequate resources in the face of donor aid cuts last year.
However, Penza said social sector spending would be unaffected by attempts to cut overall expenditure.
"Given the importance of the social sector....government will maintain the share of social sector spending at the 1996 level of 34 percent," he said.
The minister said the government would introduce an import declaration fee and increase the base tax for small businesses to 50,000 kwacha from 10,000 kwacha.
It would also limit the period for the carry forward of losses of company income tax, currently indefinite, to five years and increase rent fees on state land.
